content.text:
The behavior is intentional in the current implementation. [PR #55](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/55) says “Party amounts appear on hover, keyboard focus or tap.” Existing tests explicitly cover those behaviors.

[FunderSummary.svelte](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/FunderSummary.svelte:107) makes every pie segment a keyboard-focusable SVG button. Pointer entry, focus, click and Enter/Space all call `show()`. `show()` cancels pending dismissal and stores the tooltip’s party index and screen coordinates. Leaving schedules dismissal after 120 ms. Entering the tooltip cancels that timer, so users can move onto it. Touch taps toggle it. Outside clicks, Escape, resize and chart movement dismiss it.

The outline comes from the segment’s focusability and [styles.css](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/styles.css:1210), which explicitly outlines `g:focus-visible`. Clicking can focus the segment and invokes `show()` again. Source confirms multiple activation paths; it does not prove that focus alone keeps the tooltip open after an ordinary mouse exit, because `onmouseleave` still schedules dismissal. Runtime reproduction should establish the exact persistence sequence.

For strictly hover-only pie behavior, remove segment button semantics, tab stops and focus/click/keyboard/touch activation handlers together. Retain pointer hover, delayed dismissal, tooltip hover retention and Escape. Remove the segment focus-outline rule. Hiding the outline alone would leave the unwanted activation behavior intact.

The legend is a separate scope choice. Keeping its existing keyboard/touch controls preserves access to negative and unavailable totals, which have no pie segment. Tests at `frontend/tests/entity-details.spec.ts:1110–1162` cover segment focus and touch and would need updating for the requested behavior. No edits made.
